    return api.orders.handle_create({"customer_id": customer_id,
                                     "items": [{"sku": s, "quantity": q} for s, q in items]})


def test_order_history_unknown_customer_is_404(shop):
    response = shop.insights.handle_order_history("nobody")
    assert response.status == 404
    assert response.body == {"error": "customer not found"}


def test_order_history_empty_for_customer_without_orders(shop):
    response = shop.insights.handle_order_history("c1")
    assert response.status == 200
    assert response.body == {"customer_id": "c1", "orders": []}


def test_order_history_newest_first_with_status(shop):
    first = order(shop, "c1", ("BOOK", 1)).body["order_id"]
    cancelled = order(shop, "c1", ("PEN", 1)).body["order_id"]
    shop.orders.handle_cancel(cancelled)
    other = order(shop, "c2", ("PEN", 2)).body["order_id"]
    newest = order(shop, "c1", ("PEN", 2)).body["order_id"]

    body = shop.insights.handle_order_history("c1").body
    assert body["customer_id"] == "c1"
    assert body["orders"] == [
        {"order_id": newest, "status": "placed", "total_cents": 600},
        {"order_id": cancelled, "status": "cancelled", "total_cents": 300},
        {"order_id": first, "status": "placed", "total_cents": 2500},

    order(shop, "c2", ("PEN", 1))
    body = shop.insights.handle_order_history("c2").body
    assert [o["total_cents"] for o in body["orders"]] == [300]

- **`src/orders/application/order_service.py`**: new `OrderService.order_history(customer_id)`. It raises `CustomerNotFound` for unknown customers, and otherwise returns summaries newest first, using the same `summarize` path as `handle_get`, so `total_cents` includes the discount and cancelled orders are kept. The discount and ordering rules live here, not in the controller.
- **`src/orders/controllers/customer_insights.py`** (new): `CustomerInsightsController.handle_order_history`.
